Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated decision follow-up — latency/throughput (FinPay)

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today plus a couple of follow-ups so we can recommend the right deployment path.

TL;DR recommendation: based on the latency targets you mentioned (p50 ~2ms, p95 <10ms) and the expected peak traffic profile, we should evaluate Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) as the baseline. Hosted API is possible for low-to-medium sustained QPS but will likely struggle to meet consistent p95 SLOs at the scale you described without committed capacity.

Call notes:
- Use case: real-time fraud scoring for checkout (sub-50ms end-to-end requirement).
- Traffic pattern: sustained daytime traffic ~300–400 QPS, peak bursts up to ~800–1,000 QPS for 10–15 minute windows.
- Latency target: p50 ~2ms, p95 <10ms for model scoring only (network + client add ~10–20ms).
- Data sensitivity: low PII, company prefers VPC/private peering but okay starting in hosted environment for PoC if isolation is handled.

Why Dedicated looks like the right fit now:
- Predictable throughput: dedicated GPU pools give you guaranteed concurrent capacity to hit p95 targets during sustained load.
- Control over batching and kernel configuration: we can tune batching to optimize p50 while keeping p95 under control for tails.
- Autoscaling/burst: can configure reserved capacity + burst to handle those 800–1,000 QPS spikes without cold-starts.

When Hosted API could work:
- If initial PoC traffic is <200 QPS sustained and peak bursts are small, Hosted is fastest to get started and lower maintenance.
- We can recommend performance guardrails, but Hosted has fewer guarantees on latency at high sustained QPS.

Follow-ups / asks for you (so we can size and price):
1) Can you confirm expected sustained QPS (avg daytime) and absolute peak QPS for release 1?
2) Do you have an internal SLO for p95 model latency (is <10ms a hard requirement)?
3) Any procurement constraints / timing (e.g., vendor checklist, SOC2 attestation deadlines)?

Attached: finpay_latency_report.csv (your sample traces), redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-onepager.pdf (short overview).

Next steps I propose:
- You send confirmed QPS numbers (1–2 bullets).
- We prepare an initial Dedicated config (500 sustained QPS baseline w/ 2x burst) + Hosted fallback cost comparison and a one-page rollout plan.
- Quick technical PoC: 2–3 days to spin up a dedicated pool in our sandbox and run your sample traces.

Happy to jump on a 15-minute follow if helpful.

—

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated decision follow-up — latency/throughput (FinPay)

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap and the one-pager is useful. A few clarifying items: 

- Sustained QPS: our current baseline for the fraud scorer is about 350 QPS daytime (US market), with expected steady growth.
- Peak: historically we see short spikes ~800 QPS during marketing promos; worst-case planning number would be 1,000 QPS for a few minutes.
- p95 requirement: we want p95 model latency <=10ms; p50 1–3ms is ideal.
- Procurement: we need SOC2 + pen test attestation before we move to a contract, and procurement cycle is typically 4–6 weeks. We can start a PoC earlier though.

Question on Dedicated sizing: in your note you suggested 500 sustained QPS baseline — is that the starting config you’d price? What would the delta be to cover 1,000 QPS peaks (burst config) and can we have automatic fallback to Hosted if Dedicated has capacity issues?

Also curious about monitoring — do you provide token-level latency/cost traces per route (we need to integrate with our telemetry)?

On timing, we can confirm numbers internally by tomorrow morning. Can you also include an estimated monthly cost range for the 500 sustained + 2x burst config in the PoC?

—Alex
